criteria.title: Group responsibilities by cohesion and ownership. - capstone composition
criteria.task: Design two concrete decompositions of the shared telemetry system: synchronous parser-to-sink calls and an owned-message queue between core and adapters. Use the two-session/three-queue/one-active contract. Draw every borrow, ownership transfer and failure return; identify which component owns wire validity, authorization, queue policy and external effects. Show why a blocked sink must not retain a borrowed parser scratch pointer.

criteria.title: Identify assets, trust boundaries, attacker-controlled input, and environmental faults. - capstone composition
criteria.task: For the original local telemetry service, define assets as synthetic accepted-message counter, bounded queue and disposable output file. Give the adversary arbitrary bounded frame bytes, request timing and CRC recomputation, but no control of the trusted authorization argument. Demonstrate a valid CRC frame denied without effects; compare accidental bit corruption, deliberate valid input and slow-consumer failure.

security.scope: Original local teaching service/firmware models and synthetic data only. Physical work is a separately authorized dedicated-board task, not performed by authoring.
security.target: Original telemetry service, scripted adapter or firmware state model named in this exact criterion.
security.environment: C17 local process/model with bounded input and storage; native kernel work only in a disposable VM and physical work only on a dedicated teaching target when separately authorized.
security.attacker_capabilities: Chooses synthetic frame bytes, request timing, allowed completion order and explicitly injected model faults. Does not control trusted authorization or host security policy.
security.isolation: No external target, deployed equipment, credentials or real data; use private temporary files and process-local pipes/socket pairs. Never disable host mitigations or execute an invalid native control transfer.
security.defect: CRC-valid data is authentic or authorized.
security.exposing_transition: For the original local telemetry service, define assets as synthetic accepted-message counter, bounded queue and disposable output file. Give the adversary arbitrary bounded frame bytes, request timing and CRC recomputation, but no control of the trusted authorization argument. Demonstrate a valid CRC frame denied without effects; compare accidental bit corruption, deliberate valid input and slow-consumer failure.
security.exploitability_limits: Only the stated synthetic effect, lifetime/resource violation or model selection error is claimed. A crash/diagnostic is not arbitrary code execution; physical/security enforcement is not inferred from a host model.
security.success_condition: Unauthorized valid frames do not increment the counter or enter the queue; bad CRC emits no message; authorized valid input still works. The attack changes only synthetic local state in the flawed control.
security.repair: Restore the exact admission, ownership, progress, isolation or validity invariant specified in the task; compare the original local defective control with the corrected implementation.
security.regression: Check Unauthorized valid frames do not increment the counter or enter the queue; bad CRC emits no message; authorized valid input still works. The attack changes only synthetic local state in the flawed control. Also retain an ordinary valid successful workflow and a deliberately faulty control that fails for the intended semantic reason.
security.residual_limits: Same-process memory discipline, actual adapter behavior, physical hardware, tool/model assumptions and unsupported threat capabilities remain separately bounded.
